passages.note: Bill overview lists Carbone as Prime sponsor of HB2720, the ADU zoning-deregulation bill.
House Final Reading vote detail shows Carbone voting Y on final passage, 35-22-3-0-0.

passages.provision_quote: A municipality with a population of more than seventy-five thousand persons shall adopt regulations that allow on any lot or parcel where a single-family dwelling is allowed all of the following: 1. At least one attached and one detached accessory dwelling unit as a permitted use.
passages.note: Enacted Chapter 196 text mandates municipalities allow ADUs as a permitted use and bars added zoning barriers (parking, design-matching, setbacks).

rows.reasoning: As prime sponsor of HB2720 (2024) and by voting Y on its 35-22-3-0-0 final House passage, Carbone acted to require municipalities to permit accessory dwelling units as a permitted use by right and to bar added zoning barriers such as extra parking, design-matching requirements, and tighter setbacks, matching rung 5's text to 'rely on the market to set prices and supply — at most, cut the regulations and zoning limits that block private building.' The bill builds no public housing, sets no binding rent or affordability mandates, and offers no subsidy, ruling out rungs 1 through 4.
